newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait NIC looks at second Proclad plant in Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait NIC looks at second Proclad plant in Gulf.

text.p: The Kuwait-based National Industries Co NIC said on Tuesday it would either build the Gulf's second oil well Christmas tree treatment plant or expand its existing one in Abu Dhabi.
"Christmas trees" are above-ground valve assemblies that control the flow of oil and gas from producing wells.
"The debate now is to make the Abu Dhabi plant bigger or to put a second plant" in the Gulf region, NIC's Chief General Manager Robert Kottritsch told Reuters.

NIC, which last year paid $154 million for the acquisition of the Birmingham-based BI Group PLC, will officially open in October the Abu Dhabi plant which is using BI technology, Proclad, to coat the wellhead production devices.
He said the Abu Dhabi plant, due to start operations in August, had a committed work book to coat and treat Christmas trees for erosion and corrosion.

Regional oil firms, including from Iran and global giant Saudi Aramco, were sending their Christmas trees for treatment at BI facilities in Britain and the United States, making the decision to build a Proclad plant in the Gulf a viable one.
"But the difficulty of a second plant is you have to clone all the technology expertise...It requires very special quality and it takes a long time to train people on that," said Kottritsch.
The plant itself "is not very expensive but profitability is very high" in a region which controls more some 70 percent of the world's proven oil reserves.

NIC, the region's second largest non-oil sector industrial group after the much larger global giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), is also in the final selection process for suppliers of equipment for its second white building stone plant in Kuwait.
He said the contract would be worth around $7 million for the plant which will break ground before the end of the year for the production of some 1,000 cubic metres a day.
NIC, which has an amibitious plan to increase its industrial assets to $1 billion by 2005 from over $300 million, on Tuesday reported a 27 percent rise in 1996 net profit to $84 million.
